name: Pilocytic Astrocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of biphasic pattern with compacted bipolar cells and loose microcystic areas
Identification of Rosenthal fibers on histological examination
MRI showing cystic lesion with an enhancing mural nodule, typically in cerebellum or optic pathways
Presence of KIAA1549-BRAF fusion or BRAF V600E mutation (supportive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic biphasic pattern and Rosenthal fibers, supported by typical MRI findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for BRAF alterations can aid diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visual field defects due to optic pathway involvement
searchTerms: blind spots from optic nerve damage
visual field loss due to nerve involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Headache with signs of increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: headache with high brain pressure signs

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure
weakness on one side of body

occasional.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction (e.g., precocious puberty) in hypothalamic tumors
searchTerms: abnormal hormone levels causing early sexual development
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

imaging: MRI showing cystic lesion with enhancing mural nodule, often in cerebellum or optic pathways
other: Histopathology demonstrating biphasic pattern and Rosenthal fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Monomorphous piloid cells without Rosenthal fibers
Diffuse infiltration without well-demarcated cystic nodule
Absence of biphasic pattern and Rosenthal fibers

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (severe headache, vomiting, papilledema)
New onset seizures or focal neurological deficits
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Louis DN, et al. The 2016 World Health Organization Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary. Acta Neuropathol. 2016.
